In response, New Zealand countered with 489/10 (162.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Kane Williamson 176 (285b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Kane Williamson delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (176 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 48%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, New Zealand faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by Colin Grandhomme (57 Runs & 3 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While New Zealand produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
